title: librarian-consolidation
intention: The librarian consolidates redundant memories into fewer, stronger retrievals — the largest measured lever in the field (Generative Agents ablation d=8.16).
why: The biggest measured lever in the field: Generative Agents ablation d=8.16, the largest clean effect in the corpus (arXiv 2304.03442). A-Mem Zettelkasten-style linking (new notes link to AND UPDATE old ones): multi-hop F1 9.09->39.41, 6-7x token cut (arXiv 2502.12110). BUT: MemBench showed reflection-heavy architectures DEGRADE under prolonged interaction while plain retrieval holds (arXiv 2506.21605). The degradation happens because ungated consolidation rots — the tenure loop is the gate. A consolidation that must earn standing like any other node cannot rot the graph because the same decay/invalidation physics apply to it. The lived symptom: the librarian has 70 nodes that are all low-level fragments; nobody synthesizes them into the higher-level understanding that would resolve a broader question in one walk.
traces_to: Telos 1 — inference compilation: consolidation compiles many retrievals into fewer, stronger ones
Law 1 — spent on the novel: the largest clean effect size in the Generative Agents ablation

falsifier.proves_green: A consolidation mechanism that fires on promotion events, synthesizes a higher-level node from a cluster, deposits it as 'hypothesis', and links to source nodes. Proof teeth: (1) a promotion event triggers consolidation and deposits a new node with provenance.source='consolidated'; (2) the consolidated node enters at standing 'hypothesis', never 'earned'; (3) the consolidated node's provenance.source_nodes lists all source node_ids (derivation traceable); (4) a consolidation-of-consolidation is refused unless the consolidated source nodes have themselves earned standing; (5) a consolidation that fires on a timer/daemon instead of a promotion event reds.
falsifier.proves_red: RED on any of: (1) a consolidation node enters at standing 'earned' instead of 'hypothesis'; (2) consolidation fires on a timer/daemon instead of an event; (3) the synthesized node does not link to its source nodes (derivation is untraceable); (4) a consolidation of consolidated nodes (recursive reflection) is not gated by the same tenure physics — ungated recursion is the rot path; (5) consolidation runs when the source nodes are all from the same crossing (this is a summary, not a consolidation — crossing honesty applies).

how.trigger: The PROMOTION EVENT — LibrarianDevice.emit('resolve', ..., promoted=N) where N > 0. Promotion means independent crossings corroborated a node past PROMOTION_THRESHOLD, so it is the natural 'enough evidence to synthesize' signal. The consolidation fires as a post-resolution callback, not a daemon. A session-close event is a secondary trigger for deposited-but-unresolved clusters (nodes landed but no promotion happened).
how.mechanism: On trigger: (1) walk the promoted node's neighbors (existing neighbors() call, k=10) to find the cluster. (2) Filter to nodes at standing 'earned' or 'hypothesis' with attestations — the synthesis should draw on nodes that have independent reach, not unattested fragments. (3) Call inference (resolve with kind='generate') with a consolidation prompt: the cluster's contents, asking for ONE higher-level statement that subsumes them. (4) Deposit the synthesized statement as a new node via deposit() with provenance type 'consolidated'. (5) Link the consolidated node to each source node via link() — the derivation is traceable.
how.recursive_gate: A consolidated node is born 'hypothesis' like everything else. It can itself be consolidated (a higher-level synthesis of syntheses), but only after it independently earns standing through the tenure loop — same PROMOTION_THRESHOLD, same DECAY_HORIZON. Ungated recursion is the rot path (MemBench degradation); the tenure loop IS the gate. The falsifier (4) pins this: a consolidation of consolidated nodes without earned standing is refused.
how.integration_point: In loop.py's _tenure_on_resolution(), after the promoted list is computed. If promoted is non-empty, call a consolidate() function that runs the mechanism above. The consolidation deposit fires LibrarianDevice.emit('deposit') normally — the system sees it as another crossing, not a special event. The consolidation's own nodes enter the tenure loop and are subject to the same decay, corroboration, and refutation as any other node.
how.cost_bound: One inference call per promotion event (bounded: promotions are rare — PROMOTION_THRESHOLD=2 distinct crossings). The neighbor walk is a read, not inference. The synthesis prompt is one generate call. A promotion event that triggers consolidation on N nodes costs O(1) inference + O(N) deposit writes.
